content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses a single verse's internal qualification to call the point UNDERDETERMINED, which is what K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"The phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.' I weighed whether a verse with two senses is open/UNDERDETERMINED versus the rule's reading that both senses stand and the verse is not open.","why":"The judge assigns UNDERDETERMINED to Luke 2:48-49 because 'thy father' is qualified by 'my Father's business,' but K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses at once is not open and both senses stand."}
